headline_marked: NATO announces [[multi-billion dollar arms deals]] ahead of Trump summit
headline: NATO announces multi-billion dollar arms deals ahead of Trump summit
summary: European nations pledge increased defense spending, aiming to bolster the alliance and address security concerns amid rising geopolitical tensions. The deals are set to be announced before a crucial meeting with the US President.
details: NATO member states are set to announce multi-billion dollar arms deals ahead of a summit meeting with US President Donald Trump. The announcements are scheduled for Tuesday at NATO's defense industry forum in Ankara, Turkey. This move aims to demonstrate Europe's commitment to increased defense spending.

NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg highlighted that European countries have significantly boosted their defense expenditures. This surge is attributed to the security concerns arising from Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and sustained pressure from President Trump.

Stoltenberg stated that the alliance is building a partnership where the US will perceive it as a fair contribution. According to NATO data, the combined defense spending of European members and Canada is projected to exceed $570 billion in 2025, a real-term increase of nearly 20% from the previous year, amounting to approximately $90 billion.

Reuters reports, citing multiple sources, that Trump may offer positive assurances to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan regarding Turkey's potential return to the US F-35 stealth fighter jet program. The US had previously sanctioned Turkey and removed it from the F-35 program in 2019 after Turkey acquired Russia's S-400 missile defense system.

The summit is also expected to reaffirm support for Ukraine, with a potential commitment of €70 billion in aid this year. While details of the major arms deals remain undisclosed, the Netherlands is expected to announce defense projects valued at over €3 billion.
Additionally, NATO is planning to procure new surveillance aircraft. Canada has also decided to purchase up to 12 submarines from Germany's TKMS.

headline: Malaysia's labor market reopens for Bangladeshi workers after govt announcement
summary: The Malaysian labor market officially reopened for Bangladeshi workers on Monday, July 6, according to the Minister of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment. The minister also hinted at upcoming good news regarding labor markets in the Middle East and J
details: The Malaysian labor market has officially reopened for workers from Bangladesh starting Monday, July 6. The announcement was made by Minister of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment, Arifurul Haque Chowdhury, on Tuesday, July 7, while speaking at the Sylhet Circuit House.

The minister expressed optimism about securing new labor market opportunities in the Middle East and Japan, stating that positive news is expected soon. He also mentioned ongoing discussions and potential collaborations with Mauritius.

Earlier, the minister held a courtesy meeting with the US Ambassador, Brent T. Christensen, on the occasion of America's 250th anniversary. The meeting was followed by a cultural event at the historic Ali Amjad Watch in Sylhet, where discussions also touched upon Bangladesh's potential in the global labor market.
caption:
Good news for job seekers! Malaysia's labor market has officially reopened for Bangladeshi workers starting July 6.

The Malaysian labor market has officially reopened for workers from Bangladesh starting Monday, July 6. The announcement was made by Minister of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment, Arifurul Haque Chowdhury, on Tuesday, July 7, while speaking at the Sylhet Circuit House.

The minister expressed optimism about securing new labor market opportunities in the Middle East and Japan, stating that positive news is expected soon. He also mentioned ongoing discussions and potential collaborations with Mauritius.

Earlier, the minister held a courtesy meeting with the US Ambassador, Brent T. Christensen, on the occasion of America's 250th anniversary. The meeting was followed by a cultural event at the historic Ali Amjad Watch in Sylhet, where discussions also touched upon Bangladesh's potential in the global labor market.
